title: Exterior criterion for a bounded connected graded bialgebra
statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field [def-weil-field]: in characteristic $p>0$ every element has a $p$th root. Let $H=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}H^i$ be a graded unital associative $k$-algebra, finite dimensional as a $k$-vector space, with $H^0=k\cdot1$ and $1\ne0$. Assume $xy=(-1)^{ij}yx$ for $x\in H^i,y\in H^j$. Give $H\otimes_kH$ multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=(-1)^{\deg b\deg c}ac\otimes bd$. Suppose $\Delta:H\to H\otimes_kH$ is a degree-preserving coassociative unital algebra map, and projection $\varepsilon:H\to H^0=k$ satisfies $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=\mathrm{id}_H$. Let $g\geq0$ satisfy $\dim_kH^1=g$ and $H^i=0$ for $i>g$. Then every $v\in H^1$ has $v^2=0$, and multiplication induces an isomorphism of graded $k$-algebras $\bigwedge_k^*H^1\xrightarrow{\sim}H$, sending $v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_i$ to $v_1\cdots v_i$, with the exterior algebra defined in [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra].

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, equality case, with the coassociative algebra-map and counit hypotheses made explicit. Its proof invokes Borel 1953; that structure theorem is not supplied by the existing primitive-product lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-borel-graded-bialgebra-monomial-basis] to $H$: perfectness, finite dimension, connectedness, the signed algebra-map condition, coassociativity and both counit identities are precisely the stated hypotheses. Obtain homogeneous $x_j$, positive degrees $d_j$ and heights $N_j\geq2$, with the indicated bounded ordered monomials a basis.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, proof: the Borel (1953) structure theorem and the equality-case degree argument.

proof.text: In this homogeneous basis the degree-one monomials are exactly the single generators with $d_j=1$, so their number is $g$. The basis monomial $\prod_jx_j^{N_j-1}$ is nonzero in degree $D=\sum_j(N_j-1)d_j$, hence $D\leq g$. Each of the $g$ degree-one generators contributes at least $1$ to $D$, and every additional generator contributes positively. Thus there are exactly $g$ generators, all $d_j=1$, and every $N_j=2$. The basis is therefore the squarefree ordered products of these generators. This includes $g=0$, when the basis is $\{1\}$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, proof: the Borel (1953) structure theorem and the equality-case degree argument.

proof.text: Write $v=\sum_jc_jx_j\in H^1$. Since $x_j^2=0$ and $x_ix_j+x_jx_i=0$, expansion gives $v^2=\sum_jc_j^2x_j^2+\sum_{i<j}c_ic_j(x_ix_j+x_jx_i)=0$. This uses no division by $2$, so it also proves the assertion in characteristic $2$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, proof: the Borel (1953) structure theorem and the equality-case degree argument.

proof.text: For each $i$, the product map $(v_1,\ldots,v_i)\mapsto v_1\cdots v_i$ is multilinear and alternating: move repeated factors together using the sign rule, then use $v^2=0$. By [lem-trf-exterior-power-universal-property] it factors uniquely through $\phi_i:\bigwedge_k^iH^1\to H^i$ with the displayed product formula. For $i=0$ this is $k\to H^0$, $c\mapsto c1$.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, proof: the Borel (1953) structure theorem and the equality-case degree argument.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis], the increasing wedges in the basis $x_1,\ldots,x_g$ are a basis in each exterior degree. Their images under $\phi_i$ are precisely the squarefree monomial basis in degree $i$ from Step 2, so every $\phi_i$ is bijective (both sides are zero for $i>g$). Their direct sum is unital and multiplicative: on spanning pure wedges both orders of multiplication give the same concatenated product in $H$, by [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Thus it is the asserted graded algebra isomorphism, induced by multiplication and independent of the chosen basis.
